name: Endocrinopathy with Congenital Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism as a Major Feature
aliases: Idiopathic Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism with Endocrine Dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism

criteria.description: Low serum gonadotropins (LH and FSH) with low sex steroid levels indicating hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Onset of hypogonadism symptoms during infancy or adolescence consistent with congenital etiology
Presence of anosmia or hyposmia supporting diagnosis of Kallmann syndrome subtype
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with congenital onset plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and olfactory testing aid in confirming diagnosis and subclassification.

pathognomonic.notes: Deficiency of gonadotropin secretion leading to absent or incomplete puberty
searchTerms: low sex hormone causing delayed sexual development

pathognomonic.notes: Reduced or absent sense of smell, characteristic of Kallmann syndrome subtype
searchTerms: loss or reduced sense of smell

common.symptomName: Delayed or absent secondary sexual characteristics
common.notes: Lack of pubertal development such as breast development or testicular enlargement
searchTerms: no development of secondary sexual features

common.notes: Underdeveloped penile size due to androgen deficiency
Undescended testes commonly observed in affected males
Impaired spermatogenesis or anovulation secondary to hypogonadism

occasional.notes: Osteopenia or osteoporosis due to long-standing sex steroid deficiency
Including cleft lip or palate in some genetic subtypes
Occasionally due to hypothalamic or pituitary abnormalities

searchTerms: holes or defects in heart walls

laboratory: Low serum luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH)
Low serum testosterone in males or estradiol in females
Normal or low-normal pituitary hormone levels excluding other pituitary deficiencies
imaging: MRI showing hypoplastic or absent olfactory bulbs and tracts
Normal pituitary gland morphology in most cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in KAL1, FGFR1, PROKR2, GNRHR, and other related genes
other: Olfactory testing confirming anosmia or hyposmia
Bone density scans showing osteopenia or osteoporosis

distinguishingFeatures: Spontaneous puberty onset later in adolescence

redFlags: Failure to initiate puberty by age 14 in males or 13 in females
Presence of anosmia or hyposmia in a patient with delayed puberty
Cryptorchidism or micropenis in male infants
references: Dwyer AA, Raivio T. Congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Endocr Dev. 2019;36:1-15.
